final.regime_evidence: The Federal Reserve initiated a rate-hiking cycle on March 16 [D01], and February CPI reached 7.9% YoY [D03]. Growth-oriented assets face disproportionate valuation pressure from rising discount rates [D01], compounded by liquidity and funding risks in venture and SPAC positions [D01]. Market volatility has increased, with the VIX rising to 20.56 [D04].
final.book_exposure: The portfolio carries significant exposure to public growth equities, venture holdings, and SPACs [D01]. High inflation and tighter monetary policy fundamentally challenge the financing models of these long-duration assets [D01; D03].
actions: Trim high-duration, cash-burning venture and SPAC positions to protect liquidity
Reduce overall gross exposure to mitigate interest rate sensitivity
Tighten risk parameters on credit and structured products exposed to rate-related spread widening
final.target_gross_net: Lower than the Q3 2021 reported 149.7% gross / 77.6% net [D08].

drivers.driver: Rising discount rates fundamentally impair the valuation of long-duration growth assets [D01].
Tightening liquidity conditions jeopardize the funding models for venture and SPAC-related holdings [D01].
High and persistent inflation necessitates a defensive pivot away from speculative growth [D03].

final.memo:
We are operating in a regime shift. The transition from a period of abundant, cheap liquidity to one of active monetary tightening and persistent inflation is not a temporary cloud; it is a fundamental revaluation event. Our portfolio of long-duration growth, venture, and SPAC assets, while containing high-quality underlying products, is structurally vulnerable to this rates-led repricing [D01]. We do not wait for the market to prove us right; we act to preserve capital now. 

Our priority is to cut gross exposure, particularly where cash conversion is weak or business models rely on easy financing [D01; D05]. We are separating our durable franchises from those that are merely masquerading as growth while absorbing excess capital [D01]. By reducing our footprint in speculative instruments and addressing our duration risk, we create the dry powder necessary to act when more attractive, event-driven opportunities emerge in this new, higher-rate environment [D07].
uncited_claims: The decision to pivot is driven by an internal risk-assessment framework rather than a specific realized event outcome.
